inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL CTE aggregates monthly account activity, then self-joins the monthly result and uses PERIOD_DIFF to retain consecutive months.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored credit-threshold audit. Fixed YYYYMM periods, grouped credit totals, a HAVING threshold, and a self-join identify adjacent qualifying months; account names, values, and reporting purpose are new.

fixture_notes: Account 11 has qualifying December 2023 and January 2024 credit months, exposing a year boundary. Account 12 has a two-month gap, and account 13 has a below-threshold first month; neither produces an adjacent-month result.
determinism_notes: Account IDs and period codes are fixed, grouped output has explicit account/period ordering, and no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE credit_entries (entry_id INT PRIMARY KEY, account_id INT NOT NULL, period_code INT NOT NULL, entry_kind VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, amount DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: WITH qualifying_months AS (SELECT account_id, period_code, SUM(amount) AS monthly_credit FROM credit_entries WHERE entry_kind = 'credit' GROUP BY account_id, period_code HAVING SUM(amount) > 1000) SELECT current_month.account_id, current_month.period_code AS first_period, next_month.period_code AS next_period, PERIOD_DIFF(next_month.period_code, current_month.period_code) AS month_gap FROM qualifying_months current_month INNER JOIN qualifying_months next_month ON next_month.account_id = current_month.account_id WHERE PERIOD_DIFF(next_month.period_code, current_month.period_code) = 1 ORDER BY current_month.account_id, current_month.period_code

checks.sql: SELECT entry_id, account_id, period_code, entry_kind, amount FROM credit_entries ORDER BY entry_id
